issues.description: reload() is not atomic: clear-then-parse leaves manager empty/half-populated if parsing fails mid-reload.
issues.detail: reload() clears marks before parsing the new file. If _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises, the user is left with an empty or partial mark set and the 'changed' signal semantics are corrupted. Build the new OrderedDict as a value first, then swap-and-emit once on success. Preserve prior state on failure.

issues.description: New command names break the singular convention used by sibling commands.
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark_save, quickmark_add, quickmark_load, bookmark_add (singular, exposed as :quickmark-* / :bookmark-*). The patch introduces plural quickmarks_reload / bookmarks_reload. Rename to quickmark_reload / bookmark_reload and update the feature files to match the surrounding voice.

issues.description: reload() now emits 'changed' during __init__, a behavior change smuggled into a refactor.
issues.detail: The old __init__ did not emit changed on initial load; the new __init__ calls reload() which unconditionally emits. Either suppress the signal on initial load or extract a pure _parse_file helper that both __init__ and reload consume without the clear/emit dance. Make the decision deliberate, not incidental.

issues.description: Unit test only covers happy-path replacement; doesn't verify clear semantics or failure mode.
issues.detail: test_reload writes one entry, reloads, and checks contents. It doesn't verify that entries removed on disk disappear from memory, that multiple entries load correctly, or what happens when the file is malformed mid-reload. The clear() is load-bearing and unverified, and the failure contract is part of the public reload API now.

issues.description: Patch combines a refactor and two user-facing commands; should be split for bisectability.
issues.detail: The urlmarks.reload() extraction, the quickmark-reload command, and the bookmark-reload command are three independent changes. Landing them as one commit makes future bisects land on a commit that does three things. Split into refactor + command + command.

issues.description: Feature test scenarios for the new commands are unnamed.
issues.detail: Every other Scenario in urlmarks.feature has a descriptive title (e.g., 'Scenario: Saving a quickmark'). The two new scenarios are anonymous. Name them 'Scenario: Reloading bookmarks' and 'Scenario: Reloading quickmarks' to match the file's voice.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a small, mostly correct patch with three concrete issues to fix before merge. The dominant concern is that reload() complects clearing, parsing, and signaling without an atomic boundary, so a mid-reload parse error leaves the manager in a broken state — the fix is to build the new OrderedDict as a value and swap on success. Second, the new command names (quickmarks_reload, bookmarks_reload) break the singular convention of every sibling command in the file and should be renamed. Third, calling reload() from __init__ silently introduces a 'changed' emit on initial construction that the old code deliberately avoided. Tests and patch hygiene (split commits, named scenarios, broader assertions) are the remaining cleanup.
